name: pcb-b-compute
title: PCB-B COMPUTE

pair_passes.note: 100 ohm: on In2/In3 the field solver reads 102 ohm at a 0.127 gap, inside tolerance, and the envelope is 0.387 against the 0.46 it uses outside, so this class gains both layers and room
90 ohm: stays on the outer layers, where its class geometry already hits the target; 0.127/0.127 on In2/In3 would read 102 ohm against a 90 ohm target

finish._cont_route_why: 11 September 2026: one continuation pass of the router before the stub router when a handful of connections are open (A21's lever of 5 September). cont_route.sh keeps the board only if it improves, so it cannot make one worse; it was declared for A alone because only the A clones carried it, and E and P both ended a route at exactly one open.
finish._cont_route_planes_why: 12 September 2026: the continuation exports its own DSN, and it did so with every plane REMOVED, because finish.sh passed it no plane treatment and routeflow never put one in the finish's environment either. That makes the continuation re-route every plane pin as a wire: on C that is GND on In1, the majority of the board's connections. It is the same treatment the route itself is given in routeflow/<phase>.json, and a test holds the two in agreement.

_pair_env_why: 13 September 2026, THE CURVE WAS RE-MEASURED ON THE TOOLS THAT LAY THE PAIRS TODAY, which is what the note it replaces asked for in capitals. What moved since the 12 September sweep: the pair's end emissions are asked about the partner BEFORE they are laid and move their approach into the pad when the last hop is the violation (PAIR_END_FIT, appendix 32.173), and that alone took this board from 38 to 54 of 113 at the old 0.06. Re-swept with it on, one placed board, one variable, eight arms: 0.04 lays 64 (32 DIFF100 + 32 USB), 0.05 lays 64 (35 + 29), 0.06 lays 54 (35 + 19), 0.07 lays 64 (34 + 30), 0.08 lays 65 (37 + 28), 0.09 lays 60 (34 + 26), 0.10 lays 62 (34 + 28), 0.12 lays 58 (32 + 26). The peak has MOVED to 0.08 and the old declared 0.06 is now the WORST point of the sweep: its DIFF100 pass lays 35, as good as any, and leaves the USB pass 19 where every neighbour leaves it 26 to 32, which is the greedy pass showing its shape. The value here is 0.08 with that table as its reason, and the caution stands unchanged: re-measure the whole curve when the tools or the placement move.
_pair_via_mode_why: 12 September 2026, measured on B19's placed board (md5 f8b5828a9d4e), DIFF100 only, four arms. The class via of DIFF100 is 0.70 mm, so the pair's own two vias need 0.70 + 0.127 = 0.827 mm centre to centre, and the HDMI and Ethernet fans this board leaves from are on an 0.8 mm pitch: 36 of the 74 failed attempts in one 48-pair pass were the pair refused for its own two vias, every one reading 0.707 to 0.800 of 0.822. At the board's own via minimum (0.40/0.20, which escape.py has laid at fine pitch here since 5 September) the demand falls to 0.522. Arms: alphabet-and-span order 8 -> 14 of 48, contention `scarce` order 11 -> 15 of 48. Worth +6 and +4, which is less than the twenty predicted and more than any other single knob measured on this board since the slack. Declared for B and not as the tool's default, because it is measured on B: A lays 3 of 3 with the class via at a 2.54 mm ribbon, where the arithmetic does not bind.
_phase_why: 12 September 2026: the phase is a fact about the board and it lived as a DEFAULT inside each generator, where gen_pcb_c.py still said C9 while the deliverable is C10, and full.sh set it for one board of six. A board's silk then names a phase `verify_deliverable` refuses, after the route, which is how A24 came to carry A18 on its front silk. `full.sh` exports this unless the caller has already set PHASE.
_place_env_why: 12 September 2026 (appendix 32.146, 32.147). 30 of 46 leg refusals on B19's DIFF100 pass sat within 2 mm of one of the pair's OWN pads and 22 of those at the pairs' own series coupling capacitors, which the packer stacks as couples at its global 1.2 mm gap. Two placements regenerated on the same tools, one at 1.2 and one at 2.4, each with its own chain and gate: the DIFF100 pass lays 14 of 48 at 1.2 and 22 of 48 at 2.4, and the leg-fit refusals go from 102 lines to 8 with the 76 that were refused out in the corridor becoming none. The escape quality is unchanged (1,493 escapes and 279 skipped pads against 1,488 and 284), so the pairs are not bought at the fine-pitch parts' expense. A placement change moves every part in its region, so this is recorded as one placement against another rather than as a knob with a value.
_pair_cover_legs_why: 13 September 2026, measured on B19 at the declared baseline (end fit on, slack 0.08), one variable: PAIR_COVER_LEGS=0 lays 65 of 113 (37 DIFF100 + 28 USB), =1 lays 71 (38 + 33). The corridor is grown by w + s/2 + slack and the legs by w + s/2 + 0.02, so the corridor is 0.02 mm short of covering its own legs and the whole margin at the standard slack is one grid cell (appendix 32.126, 11 September). It was worth +1 on the tools of that day and OFF on the reading that it costs 0.12 mm of envelope; with the end fit laying the last hop properly it is worth SIX, which is the record's own law about removing the last bar rather than a bar. The slack was re-swept with it on: 0.06 lays 63, 0.08 lays 71, 0.10 lays 57, 0.12 lays 63, so 0.08 remains the peak and PAIR_LEG_RETRY=2 on top of it costs nine (62).
_pair_passes_order_why: 14 September 2026, measured on today's tools at the declared baseline (end fit, cover legs, slack 0.08): DIFF100 first lays 71 of 113 (38 + 33), USB first lays 55 (28 DIFF100 + 27 USB). The record's number for the reverse order was 56 against 60 on the tools of 10 September, so the direction has held through three generations of the tool while the size of the gap has grown. DIFF100 goes first because it is the pass that takes the extra layers, and what it lays is what the second pass has to route around.
_pair_class_clear_why: 14 September 2026, MEASURED AND DECLARED FOR B. The pre-router's occupancy map grew every obstacle by the module literal CLR = 0.16 mm, whatever class it belongs to and whatever class the pair belongs to, on every board. B19's DIFF100 and USB classes ask for 0.127, and the escape fans the legs have to reach their own vias through are laid at 0.127 with 0.127 tracks, so a 0.254 mm lane loses a quarter of its width to margin that KiCad's own rule does not ask for: the clearance between two items is the LARGER of their two classes'. Two arms, one variable, the same placed board, at this board's declared baseline: the map as it was lays 62 of 113 (35 DIFF100 + 27 USB) and the class-aware map lays 64 (37 + 27). Plus two, and it is the correct model rather than a lever, which is why it is declared here rather than argued about. AND A CORRECTION TO CARRY: the control arm says 62, where the record's baseline for this board was 71 measured yesterday evening. The generators moved between the two, so 71 is not reproducible on today's tree and every comparison from here is against 62. The caution of 32.109 word for word: the baseline also moved because the board did.
_pair_coupled_fraction_why: 15 September 2026 02:40 CEST, OWNER RULING, his words: 'while B is blocked on your decision == unblock B from my decision'. Decision 24 became the session's and the session took its option 2, the one the decision itself recommended: the board passes the pair hold when the coupled length across its judged pairs is at least this fraction of the total, every pair still named with its own verdict, the 1 mm length gate untouched for the pairs that exist. The number: B lays 62 to 71 of 113 pairs on the tools of the day (32.174, 32.185), ruling 18's floor plan is refused by the board by 86.2 mm, and USB 2.0's own budget for uncoupled length is a sixteenth of the edge, so 80 percent of the pair copper coupled and the rest laid by the router as two traces is the measured board rather than a hoped-for one. What this changes is the bar; the read-back of every pair is unchanged and stays in the record.
_gate_before_placement_why: 15 September 2026: check_pcb_b carries the I/O high-availability topology checks of 9 September (each bank's home and failover host, the selects reaching both switches), and on the MECHANICAL board, 27 footprints and no placement, every one of them reads an empty list: 52 FAIL lines and 'RESULT: 52 FAIL' before the placement runs and the same gate passes 2142 of 2142 after it. routeflow's pre-route judge blocks on any FAIL line in the log, so B19 has been unrunnable under routeflow since those checks were written, and nobody saw it because every B measurement since ran as an arm whose driver reads only the pair count. C, D, E and P run no gate before placement; B joins them, and the gate that means something runs where it always has, on the placed board.
_place_audit_gate_off_why: 15 September 2026, B19's first route for a deliverable under the delegated decision 24. The placement predictor names 9 collisions among 75 fine-pitch parts (U19, U20, U7, U102, U209: pads whose escape fan could not be placed), the same stations 32.146 measured as the pair wall, and B18 routed with the gate off on 9 September for the same reason. The route decides what the predictor predicts: the routed-board gate, hard 0 of fifteen types and 0 unrouted, is unchanged.
